title: local-edge-authz-fallback-draft
body:
Notes to self — rough draft for an authz + fallback design that runs at the edge (user-facing sidecar / gateway).

Goal:
- Allow low-latency authz checks for short-lived conversational sessions while providing graceful fallback when the central policy service is slow/unreachable.
- Keep rollout incremental: start with passive shadowing, then opt-in enforcement per-route.

Constraints / assumptions:
- Host environment may be a lightweight edge proxy or sidecar with limited CPU/memory (64-256MB).
- Want deterministic, auditable decision provenance for compliance teams.
- Must not add >30ms median tail to happy-path requests.

High-level flow (ASCII):

  client ---> edge-proxy ---> local-authz-adapter ---> routing-layer ---> inference-pool
                        |                 |
                        |                 v
                        |             fallback-engine (local cache, rule overrides)
                        v
                   telemetry + trace (sampled)

Design notes:
1) API shape (edge -> local authz adapter) — minimal JSON:
POST /v1/local-authz/check
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "principal": "user:1234",
  "resource": "model:llm-standard/v2",
  "action": "invoke",
  "context": {"session_id": "s-abc", "client_ip": "1.2.3.4"},
  "policies_hint": ["rate:low", "tier:free"]
}

Response: 200 OK
{ "decision": "allow" | "deny" | "defer", "source": "local|remote|cache", "meta": {"ttl_ms": 3000} }

- defer = accept a partial decision (allow with soft-rate-limit) until remote policy returns.
- source indicates provenance for auditing.

2) Local cache / fallback-engine behavior:
- LRU store keyed by (principal, resource, action) with small adaptive TTL based on recent update frequency.
- If remote is unreachable, return cached decision if TTL not expired. If no cache, use a configurable override-rule: (deny-by-default OR allow-by-safety-profile).
- Safety profile: conservative allow only for whitelisted model endpoints and authenticated tenants.

3) Update & sync protocol (sketch):
- Periodic delta sync from control-plane: compressed policy deltas (gzip) over HTTPS, incremental sequence numbers.
- Push notifications for critical revocations via long-poll/webhook to minimize time-to-revoke.
- Local adapter exposes an admin endpoint to force-refresh or evict keys.

4) Telemetry & traces:
- Every decision emits span with tags: decision, source, latency_ms, cache_hit. Sample at 5% by default but 100% for denies and defers.
- Cost attribution: annotate with route/model/token-bucket labels for later dissection in Console.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to represent composable policies (role + rate + tenant overrides) in a compact local format? (rough proto idea: triples, but need faster eval engine)
- Revocation semantics: do we prefer push-first (better revoke latency) vs pull-first (simpler infra)? Hybrid probably best.
- Performance budget: measure p50/p95 of adapter on 2 cores / 128MB; if >20ms p95, explore inlining simple rule eval or small WASM runtime.
- Security: encrypt local cache at rest, sign delta payloads, ensure replay protection (seq nums + HMAC).

Prototype CLI notes (to build):
- binary: redwood-edge-authz (go)
- config: YAML with fields: control_plane, sync_interval_ms, ttl_default_ms, fallback_mode (deny|allow|safety-profile)
- admin endpoints: /admin/metrics, /admin/evict?key=..., /admin/force-refresh

Example config snippet:
---
control_plane: https://control.redwood.example/api/policies/delta
sync_interval_ms: 60000
ttl_default_ms: 30000
fallback_mode: safety-profile
whitelist_models: ["llm-safe/v1", "embed-basic/v0"]
log_level: info
---

Quick notes on rollout plan:
- stage 0: passive shadow — local adapter logs remote decisions vs local cache for 2 weeks (compare diffs).
- stage 1: opt-in enforcement per-route via sidecar annotation.
- stage 2: global enforcement with aggressive telemetry and audit retention.

References / links:
- JIRA: INF-2319 (policy delta sync proto)
- GH: redwood/runtime#1423 (wasm rule-eval spike)
summary: Edge-side authz adapter draft: local cache + fallback, sync proto, API shapes, rollout checklist
